title: Risks, Adventures & Choices
description: From your course: phrases for taking risks, trying adventures, making choices and saying how things turned out.

items.definition: to make yourself do something unpleasant that you have been avoiding
items.example: I'd put it off for ages, but today I [bit the bullet] and booked the dentist.
items.exampleRu: Я долго откладывал, но сегодня всё-таки собрался с духом и записался к стоматологу.
collocations: bite the bullet and do sth
items.trap: Don't calque «стиснуть зубы» as 'squeeze my teeth'; the past is 'bit the bullet', not 'bited'.

items.definition: to accept an opportunity quickly and with excitement
items.example: When my boss offered me three months in our Berlin office, I [jumped at the chance].
items.exampleRu: Когда начальник предложил мне на три месяца поехать в наш берлинский офис, я тут же ухватился за эту возможность.
items.pattern: jump at the chance (to do sth / of doing sth)
items.trap: Use 'jump at', not 'catch the chance' (a calque of «ухватиться за шанс»).

items.definition: to jump from the top of a high rock, usually into water
items.example: In Croatia we [jumped off a cliff] into the sea – I screamed all the way down.
items.exampleRu: В Хорватии мы прыгнули со скалы в море – я орал, пока летел вниз.
items.trap: Use 'off' for leaving a high place: 'jump off a cliff', not 'jump with a cliff' (a calque of «со скалы»).

items.definition: to try very hard to avoid someone or something because you really don't want it
items.example: Karaoke at the Christmas party? No way, I'd [run a mile].
items.exampleRu: Караоке на новогоднем корпоративе? Ни за что, я бы сбежал без оглядки.
items.trap: Informal and usually conditional ('I'd run a mile'); it is about avoiding something, not really running.

items.definition: to make more effort than people expect from you
items.example: The hotel staff really [went the extra mile] for my mum's birthday.
items.exampleRu: Ради маминого дня рождения персонал отеля сделал гораздо больше, чем был обязан.
collocations: go the extra mile for sb
items.pattern: go the extra mile (for sb / to do sth)
items.trap: The words are fixed: 'go the extra mile', not 'go a mile' or 'make the extra mile'.

items.definition: swimming very deep under the sea with special breathing equipment
items.example: Is [deep-sea diving] safe if you've only done a beginners' course?
items.exampleRu: Глубоководный дайвинг вообще безопасен, если у тебя за плечами только курс для новичков?
items.trap: With activities use 'go' + -ing: 'go deep-sea diving', not 'go to deep-sea diving'.

items.definition: to jump from a very high place with a long elastic rope tied to your legs
items.example: Somehow my friends talked me into [doing a bungee jump] on holiday.
items.exampleRu: Не знаю как, но друзья уговорили меня прыгнуть с банджи в отпуске.
items.pattern: do a bungee jump / go bungee jumping
items.trap: Say 'do a bungee jump' or 'go bungee jumping', not 'jump a bungee'; after 'talk sb into' use -ing.

items.translation: выбрать, решиться на; «давай, вперёд» (go for it)
items.definition: to choose something from several options
items.example: We looked at three flats and in the end we [went for] the cheapest one.
items.exampleRu: Мы посмотрели три квартиры и в итоге выбрали самую дешёвую.
items.pattern: go for sth / go for it
items.trap: Don't calque «остановились на»: not 'we stopped on it'; and 'Go for it!' means «Давай, решайся!».

items.definition: to start doing or eating something with a lot of energy
items.example: We were starving after the hike and [went at] the sandwiches like animals.
items.exampleRu: После похода мы умирали с голоду и набросились на бутерброды, как звери.
items.trap: Informal; 'go at sb' can also mean to attack someone physically.

items.definition: a TV programme that films real people, not actors, in real or planned situations
items.example: Have you seen that new [reality TV show] where couples move to an island?
items.exampleRu: Ты видел то новое реалити-шоу, где пары переезжают на остров?
items.trap: Don't say just 'reality' for «реалити»: it means real life; say 'reality TV' or 'a reality show'.

items.definition: to see someone while they are doing something they shouldn't
items.example: I [caught my flatmate eating] my leftovers straight from the fridge at 2am.
items.exampleRu: Я застукал соседа по квартире, когда он в два часа ночи доедал мою еду прямо из холодильника.
items.pattern: catch sb doing sth / be caught doing sth
items.trap: Use the -ing form: 'caught him eating', not 'caught him to eat' or 'caught him eat'.

items.definition: to look at someone while they are in the middle of an action
items.example: On Sundays I love sitting in a café and [watching people walking] past.
items.exampleRu: По воскресеньям я люблю посидеть в кафе и понаблюдать за прохожими.
items.pattern: watch sb doing sth / watch sb do sth
items.trap: 'Watch sb doing' = you see part of the action, 'watch sb do' = you see all of it; never 'watch sb to do'.

items.definition: to persuade or arrange for someone to do something
items.example: It took a month, but I finally [got my landlord to fix] the boiler.
items.exampleRu: Ушёл целый месяц, но я всё-таки добился, чтобы хозяин квартиры починил бойлер.
items.trap: Unlike 'make', 'get' needs 'to': 'get him to fix it', not 'get him fix it'.
wrong: got from my landlord to fix

items.definition: to force someone to do something
items.example: My trainer [made me do] fifty burpees because I was late again.
items.exampleRu: Тренер заставил меня сделать пятьдесят бёрпи, потому что я опять опоздал.
items.pattern: make sb do sth / be made to do sth
items.trap: No 'to' in the active ('made me do', not 'made me to do'), but the passive needs it: 'I was made to do'.

items.translation: лучше уж (я бы)…, чем; предпочёл бы
items.definition: would prefer to do one thing rather than another
items.example: I [would sooner] walk home than squeeze onto that packed bus again.
items.exampleRu: Лучше уж я пойду домой пешком, чем снова буду втискиваться в этот битком набитый автобус.
items.pattern: would sooner do X than do Y
items.trap: Use the bare infinitive, as with 'would rather': 'I'd sooner walk', not 'I'd sooner to walk'.

items.definition: to like one thing or activity more than another
items.example: These days I [prefer] working from home to commuting into the office.
items.exampleRu: Сейчас мне больше нравится работать из дома, чем ездить в офис.
items.pattern: prefer sth to sth / prefer doing X to doing Y / would prefer to do sth
items.trap: Compare with 'to', not 'than': 'prefer working from home to commuting', not '…than commuting'.

items.translation: зависеть от кого-то, на чьё-то усмотрение
items.definition: if something is up to you, you are the one who decides
items.example: "Thai or Italian tonight?" "I really don't mind – it's [up to] you."
items.exampleRu: «Тайская или итальянская кухня сегодня?» – «Мне правда всё равно, решай сам».
items.pattern: it's up to sb (to do sth)
items.trap: When you let someone choose, say 'it's up to you', not 'it depends from you' (a calque of «зависит от тебя»).

items.definition: used to say that without someone or something, things would be very different
items.example: [If it wasn't for] coffee, I'd never survive Monday mornings.
items.exampleRu: Если бы не кофе, я бы ни за что не пережил утро понедельника.
items.pattern: if it wasn't/weren't for sth, … would … / if it hadn't been for sth, … would have …
items.trap: Keep the negative: 'if it wasn't for' = «если бы не», while 'if it was for' makes no sense here; 'weren't' is more formal.

items.definition: to decide not to do, go to or have something this time
items.example: I'm shattered, so I think I'll [give the gym a miss] tonight.
items.exampleRu: Я совсем без сил, так что сегодня, пожалуй, пропущу спортзал.
items.trap: British and informal; the thing you skip goes in the middle: 'give the gym a miss'.

items.definition: a group of words whose meaning is different from the meaning of each word
items.example: In today's meeting, a client used an [idiomatic phrase] I'd never heard before.
items.exampleRu: На сегодняшней встрече клиент употребил идиому, которую я раньше никогда не слышал.
items.trap: A 'phrase' is a short group of words, not a whole sentence like Russian «фраза».

items.definition: riding a strong bike with thick tyres on rough paths and hills
items.example: Last summer we went [mountain biking] in Wales, and I came home covered in mud.
items.exampleRu: Прошлым летом мы катались на горных велосипедах в Уэльсе, и домой я вернулся весь в грязи.
items.trap: Use 'go' + -ing: 'go mountain biking', not 'go to mountain biking' or 'go on mountain biking'.

items.definition: to suddenly feel very excited and full of energy, often because of danger
items.example: You [get an adrenalin rush] the second the roller coaster drops.
items.exampleRu: Как только вагончик американских горок летит вниз, получаешь мощный выброс адреналина.
items.pattern: get an adrenalin rush (from sth / from doing sth)
items.trap: Don't translate «выброс» as 'emission' (that's for gases); 'adrenaline' is also a correct British spelling.

items.definition: a hill that goes up or down very sharply
items.example: I live at the top of a really [steep hill], so who needs a gym?
items.exampleRu: Я живу на вершине очень крутого холма – кому вообще нужен спортзал?
items.trap: Don't translate «крутой» as 'cool' here: 'steep' means rising sharply, 'cool' means great.

items.definition: to start a journey
items.example: We [set off] early in the morning to avoid the traffic.
items.exampleRu: Мы выехали рано утром, чтобы не попасть в пробки.

items.definition: a type of music with strong rhythms, where players often make up the tune as they play
items.example: Cooking with some [jazz music] on in the background is my idea of relaxing.
items.exampleRu: Готовить, когда на фоне играет джаз, – вот для меня лучший отдых.
items.trap: 'Music' is uncountable: 'some jazz music', not 'a jazz music' or 'jazz musics'; natives often just say 'jazz'.

items.translation: полностью погрузиться во что-то, забыть обо всём
items.definition: to be so interested in something that you forget everything around you
items.example: Nothing helps me switch off like a crime novel – I just [lose myself in] it.
items.exampleRu: Ничто так не помогает отключиться, как детектив: я просто с головой в него ухожу.
items.trap: Match the pronoun ('I lose myself', 'she loses herself') and use 'in', not 'into'.

items.definition: to forget what time it is because you are busy or having fun
items.example: Sorry I'm late – I was chatting to my neighbour and completely [lost track of time].
items.exampleRu: Извини, что опоздал: заболтался с соседом и совсем потерял счёт времени.
items.pattern: lose track of time / lose track of sth
items.trap: No article: 'lose track of time', not 'lose the track' or 'lose the count of time' (a calque of «счёт»).

items.definition: a plan to change how a garden or outdoor area looks, with plants, paths and so on
items.example: We've just started a small [landscaping project] in the back garden – wish us luck!
items.exampleRu: Мы только что затеяли небольшой ландшафтный проект в саду за домом – пожелайте нам удачи!
items.trap: 'Landscape' is a view or the land itself; 'landscaping' is the work of designing a garden or outdoor space.

items.definition: the work of growing plants and looking after a garden
items.example: According to my mum, [gardening] is cheaper than therapy – and she's right.
items.exampleRu: Мама считает, что возиться в саду дешевле, чем ходить к психотерапевту, – и она права.
items.trap: Say 'do some gardening' or 'do the gardening', not 'make gardening'.

items.translation: с энтузиазмом взяться за дело; налетай(те)! (о еде)
items.definition: to start doing something, like work or eating, with energy and enthusiasm
items.example: Dinner's on the table, so [get stuck in] before it gets cold!
items.exampleRu: Ужин на столе, налетайте, пока не остыло!
items.pattern: get stuck in / get stuck into sth
items.trap: Informal British English; don't confuse it with 'get stuck' (= be unable to move or continue).

items.term: have the time of your life
items.ipa: hæv ðə taɪm əv jə laɪf
items.definition: to enjoy yourself very much, more than ever before
items.example: The kids [had the time of their lives] at the water park yesterday.
items.exampleRu: Вчера в аквапарке дети оторвались по полной.
items.pattern: have the time of your life
items.trap: For a group say 'they had the time of their lives'; the verb is 'have', not 'spend'.
wrong: spent the time of their lives
had a time of their lives

items.definition: to be at the wheel of the very fast racing car used in Formula One races
items.example: It's always been my dream to [drive a Formula One car], even just for one lap.
items.exampleRu: Моя давняя мечта – прокатиться за рулём болида Формулы-1, хотя бы один круг.
items.trap: Russian «болид» is a 'racing car' or 'F1 car' in English; a 'bolide' is a meteor.
wrong: drive a car of Formula One

items.definition: worried and a bit afraid about something that is going to happen
items.example: I'm a bit [nervous about] my job interview on Monday – any tips?
items.exampleRu: Я немного нервничаю перед собеседованием в понедельник – есть советы?
items.pattern: nervous about sth / about doing sth
items.trap: It's an adjective: 'I'm nervous about it', not 'I'm nervousing' or 'nervous from it'.

items.definition: to be extremely impressed by something
items.example: The food in Lisbon was incredible – I was totally [blown away].
items.exampleRu: Еда в Лиссабоне была невероятной – я был в полном восторге.
items.trap: Use 'by' for the cause ('blown away by the view'); don't confuse it with 'blown up' (= exploded).

items.translation: опыт, который бывает раз в жизни
items.definition: something very special that you will probably only do once in your life
items.example: Seeing the Northern Lights in Norway was a [once-in-a-lifetime experience].
items.exampleRu: Увидеть северное сияние в Норвегии – такое бывает раз в жизни.
items.trap: Use hyphens before a noun ('a once-in-a-lifetime trip') but not after a verb ('it happens once in a lifetime').

items.definition: happy to try new, exciting or slightly dangerous things
items.example: My sister's far more [adventurous] than me – she'll eat absolutely anything.
items.exampleRu: Сестра гораздо смелее меня в еде – она съест абсолютно что угодно.
items.trap: It's a positive word; for a risky, dodgy plan («авантюрный») say 'risky' or 'reckless'.

items.definition: to be as good as people hoped or expected
items.example: Did the new phone [meet your expectations], or are you sending it back?
items.exampleRu: Новый телефон оправдал твои ожидания, или будешь его возвращать?
items.trap: Don't calque «оправдать ожидания» as 'justify expectations'; say 'meet' or 'live up to'.

items.definition: to be less good than people hoped or expected
items.example: Everyone raved about that new ramen place, but it [fell short of expectations].
items.exampleRu: Все расхваливали ту новую раменную, но она не оправдала ожиданий.
items.trap: Use 'of': 'fall short of expectations', not 'fall short from' or 'not justify expectations'.

items.definition: to play a fast game in which two people hit a small ball against the walls of a room
items.example: Every Wednesday after work, my colleague and I [play squash], and he always wins.
items.exampleRu: Каждую среду после работы мы с коллегой играем в сквош, и он всегда выигрывает.
items.trap: No article or preposition: 'play squash', not 'play in squash'; in the UK 'squash' is also a fruit drink mixed with water.
